Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the draft MSA and the Order Form and asked whether Redwood would accept a narrow carve-out to the liability cap for losses tied to (i) unauthorized disclosure of trade secrets and (ii) a confidentiality breach where there is verified exfiltration of PHI.

They are proposing the following high-level approach:
- Trade secrets: unlimited damages when there is willful misappropriation or forensic evidence that Redwood’s systems led to misappropriation (forensic report + chain-of-custody)
- Confidentiality (PHI): carve-out to the cap only when an audit-confirmed exfiltration occurred and notification/mitigation obligations were followed

Can your team confirm what evidence we would need to accept a carve-out like this, and whether you have standard wording? We need to finish procurement by 10/7.

Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form - request for carve-out on trade secret losses

Evelyn / Neha,

Draft proposal below — concise clause + operational checklist. This is intentionally narrow to limit open-ended exposure. Copy of redline attached as text.

Proposed new paragraph (MSA, section 9.2 Limitations):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the liability cap shall not apply to damages arising from: (a) Willful misappropriation of Customer's trade secrets by Redwood, where Customer provides (i) a forensic report prepared by an independent, mutually agreed forensic vendor demonstrating exfiltration attributable to Redwood within the Redwood runtime or APIs and (ii) demonstrable chain-of-custody for the relevant data; or (b) Unauthorized disclosure of Customer Personal Health Information (PHI) where an authorized audit confirms exfiltration and Customer has complied with the notice and cooperation obligations in Section 12.3."

Operational evidence checklist (what we would require):
- Independent forensic report (vendor pre-approved by Redwood) with signed statement of findings
- Chain-of-custody for extracted artifacts (hashes, timestamps)
- KMS and access logs showing relevant key usage and request origin within the time window
- Images or snapshots preserved within 24–72 hours of detection
- Customer notification within 7 days of detection and 30 days to provide forensic artifacts
- Mutual cooperation clause for remediation and root-cause analysis

Risk notes: For trade-secret carve-outs we should insist on a high bar (forensic vendor, narrow temporal window, and proof tying exfiltration to our runtime or API calls). We should avoid an automatic unlimited damages trigger for mere suspicion.

Attachment: Redline_Rishi_20270929.txt

- Rishi

Evelyn / Neha,

Thank you for the quick turn. Attached is a redline with two adjustments we need to see from Redwood to avoid pushback: (1) broaden the acceptable evidence to include the customer's internal audit in addition to a third-party forensic report when the scope is limited and the vendor is not available; and (2) lengthen the preservation window to 14 days for healthcare customers with complex environments.

We also included an alternative: a capped amount (e.g., 12 months of fees) for confidentiality-related unlimited damages if Redwood can provide predefined indemnity insurance thresholds and a written remediation SLA.
